title: Khasi Cradle Lullaby (Ka Jingrwai Thiah Khunlung)
cultural_context: Sung by mothers and grandmothers in village homes while rocking infants to sleep by the warmth of the central hearth fire (ka dpei).
lyrics_khasi:
Thiah suk ko khun, thiah suk ha la ka tnum,
Ka sngi ka la sep, u bnai u la wan,
Mei-rad kan pynap da u sohkymphor bad u ngap,
Thiah suk ko khun ha shadem jong i mei.

Ki sim ki la kynmaw la ki skum ha ki dieng,
Ki sniang ki masi ki la kiew sha sem,
Wat khuslai ko khun, Blei u don ha la syndah,
Dem noh la ki khmat ban iohi ia ki jingphohsniew ba thiang!
lyrics_english:
Sleep peacefully my child, sleep safe under our ancestral roof,
The golden sun has set, the silver moon has ascended the sky,
Grandmother prepares sweet wild berries and golden mountain honey,
Sleep peacefully my child upon your mother's breast.

The forest birds have returned to their nests in the high trees,
The cattle and sheep have entered their sheltered fold,
Fret not my child, Almighty God is ever near beside thee,
Close thy little eyes to behold sweetest dreams of joy!

stanzas.title: Ka Jingpynthiah ha Shadem (Resting on Mother's Chest)
stanzas.khasi:
Thiah suk ko khun, thiah suk ha la ka tnum,
Ka sngi ka la sep, u bnai u la wan,
Mei-rad kan pynap da u sohkymphor bad u ngap,
Thiah suk ko khun ha shadem jong i mei.
stanzas.english: Sleep peacefully under our roof; the sun has set, the moon has arrived. Grandmother has honey and wild berries; rest securely upon mother's chest.

vocabulary.tnum: Ancestral thatched roof representing family sanctuary
vocabulary.mei-rad: Maternal grandmother; revered elder of the matrilineage
vocabulary.ngap: Pure wild highland honey gathered from rock hives
